newsitem.title: UK: Xenova plans LSE list, 25 mln stg placement.
newsitem.headline: Xenova plans LSE list, 25 mln stg placement.

text.p: U.K. biotech group Xenova Plc said on Tuesday it intends to seek a full listing on the London Stock Exchange and is hoping to raise 25 million stg through a share placing.
Slough-based Xenova, which is already listed on the U.S.Nasdaq market, specialises in discovering drugs based on naturally-occurring organisms in plants, fungi and bacteria.
Xenova said in a statement that its share placing will be sponsored by brokers Greig Middleton & Co Ltd.
Chief executive Louis Nisbet said in a statement the listing was "a key step in the growth and development of our business."
Xenova is focusing on anti-cancer and cardiovascular drugs.

Its lead product, XR5000, completed the first round of human trials earlier this month and the company hopes it will prove effective in a wide range of cancers, including brain, skin breast and lung cancers.
The company believes XR5000 will be able to overcome resistance in some tumors to existing cancer drugs, especially in patients who have undergone chemotherapy.
Another cancer drug, XR9051 is on early stage, or Phase I, clinical trials, while a third compound aimed at deep vein thrombosis and angina is in pre-clinical trials.
Nisbet said the funds raised through the placing will be used to advance its drug pipeline and develop existing and future collaborations with other companies.
"The bulk of Xenova's operations are in the U.K, and it is appropriate for the company to seek new local shareholders to support it through the next stages of its development," he added.
